I'll start by reading the docs and looking at the data layout.

I wrote `/app/bin/tally.py` and ran it on `/app/data`. The result is saved as `/app/out/tally.json`. Both checks passed.

- **Unit tests:** `python -m unittest discover -s tests -t .` ran 4 tests, all OK.
- **Certified results:** `python tools/check_tally.py` reported 7 of 7 contests and 31 of 31 rounds matching.

The script follows the rules in `/app/docs` rather than anything specific to the current election, and it uses only the standard library. I wrote `/app/STATUS.json` with status `success`.

One thing I assumed: a `|` inside write-in text in a CSV cell would be read as a separator between marks. The docs don't say how to tell the two apart, and none of the test fixtures contain one.

command_result.command: cd /app; ls -R docs tests tools bin out 2>&1 | head -50; ls data | head -30; cat docs/overview.md

cd /app; ls data/cvr | head; ls data/cvr | wc -l; head -c 1500 data/election.json; for f in $(ls data/cvr/* | head -3); do echo == $f; head -8 $f; done; cat tests/test_tally.py | head -40; ls tests/fixtures/*/input/cvr; head -20 tools/check_tally.py
cd /app; head -12 tests/fixtures/write_ins/input/cvr/scan_0412.csv; head -12 tests/fixtures/batches/input/cvr/a.csv; head -3 tests/fixtures/batches/input/cvr/b.jsonl
cd /app; python -m unittest discover -s tests -t . 2>&1 | tail -20; mkdir -p out; python3 bin/tally.py data out/tally.json && python tools/check_tally.py

cd /app; echo '{"status": "success", "summary": "Wrote /app/bin/tally.py implementing the documented rules (batch revisions, write-ins, ranking reading, rounds, tie-breaks) and saved /app/out/tally.json; unit tests and check_tally.py pass (7/7 contests, 31/31 rounds)."}' > STATUS.json; cat STATUS.json
